intent_record.intent_summary: Treat partial I/O completion as an error condition rather than attempting to zero-fill the remaining bio, fixing incorrect handling of incomplete file I/O operations.
intent_record.what: Replaced a conditional block that advances the bio iterator and zero-fills the remaining bio with a simpler assignment that sets ret to -EIO when the return value doesn't match the expected bio size.
intent_record.how: Previously, when ret >= 0 but didn't equal the full bio size, the code would advance the bio iterator by ret bytes and zero-fill the remaining portion. Now, it treats this partial completion as an error by setting ret to -EIO, which will be handled by subsequent error checking logic instead of attempting to zero-fill the unfilled portion.

candidates.rationale: This statement is the core vulnerability. When vfs_iocb_iter_read() returns fewer bytes than requested (due to signal interruption or other partial I/O), the code advances the bio and zero-fills the remaining portion, then marks all folios as uptodate. This incorrectly treats a partial/failed I/O as successful, corrupting data by marking unread folios as uptodate.

This condition allows the vulnerable zero-fill logic to execute when partial I/O occurs. The condition treats any non-negative return value (including partial reads) as a success case that should be handled by zero-filling, rather than treating incomplete I/O as an error condition.

When vfs_iocb_iter_read() returns fewer bytes than requested (due to signal interruption), this statement allows the vulnerability to manifest by filling unread data with zeros and subsequently marking those folios as uptodate, corrupting data integrity.

This statement advances the bio iterator by the partial amount read (ret), setting up the subsequent zero_fill_bio() call to fill the remaining portion. Together with zero_fill_bio(), this creates the vulnerability by treating incomplete I/O as a recoverable condition that can be handled by advancing and zero-filling, rather than treating it as an error condition.

diff --git a/fs/erofs/fileio.c b/f
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit shows the fix being applied to `erofs_fileio_ki_complete()`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause was: incorrectly marking all folios as uptodate when `vfs_iocb_iter_read()` returns fewer bytes than requested due to signal interruption. The original buggy code (shown in the diff context) had `if (ret > 0)` which would treat partial reads as success and zero-fill the remainder, then set `ret = 0` unconditionally, causing all folios to be marked uptodate. The fix changes this logic: (1) The condition becomes `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size)` - only zero-filling when bytes are actually missing, not treating it as complete success; (2) The `ret = 0` assignment is removed, preserving the actual return value; (3) The folio marking logic now uses `erofs_onlinefolio_end(fi.folio, ret < 0, false)` which correctly passes whether there was an error (ret < 0) rather than always treating it as success. This fix properly handles the case where fewer bytes are read than requested - it zero-fills the gap but doesn't mark the operation as fully successful, allowing proper error handling downstream.
